name: Sweep unread Gmail junk to Spam with GPT-5 and a Telegram undo button

parameters.content:
## Sweep unread Gmail junk to Spam with GPT-5 and a Telegram undo button

### How it works

1. Runs on a daily schedule, or on demand from a Telegram message.
2. Reads your unread inbox, then reads your sent mail to build a list of people you actually correspond with.
3. Anyone you have written to is removed before any model call, so known contacts can never be swept.
4. GPT-5 judges only the remaining unknown senders and returns a verdict with a confidence level for each.
5. Only high confidence junk is moved. Anything borderline stays in your inbox and is counted in the report.
6. The undo record is written BEFORE anything moves, so a failure later still leaves the mail recoverable.
7. Matching mail is moved to Spam through the Gmail API, removing the inbox and unread labels.
8. Telegram gets a list of what moved and why, with a single button that puts every message back.
9. Each run is logged to a Google Sheet, including the quiet runs where nothing matched.

### Setup steps

- [ ] Create a Telegram bot with @BotFather and add the token as a Telegram credential.
- [ ] Add a Gmail OAuth2 credential. The workflow needs permission to read and modify labels.
- [ ] Add an OpenAI credential for the classifier.
- [ ] Add a Google Sheets credential, then pick a spreadsheet and tab in both Log nodes.
- [ ] Set admin_chat_id in the Config node so the scheduled run knows where to send.
- [ ] Run it once manually and check what it would move before trusting the schedule.

### Customization

inbox_query is a normal Gmail search string. Narrow or widen what gets considered.

max_moves_per_run caps how much a single run can move, so a bad day stays small.

undo_window_days controls how long an undo batch stays available. Gmail deletes spam after 30 days regardless.

sent_lookback decides how far back the contact protection looks. A longer window protects more people.

The confidence bar is in the Resolve Junk node. It only accepts high confidence; loosening it will move more mail.

Change the schedule, or delete that trigger if you only want to sweep on demand.

## Triggers and settings
The daily schedule, or a Telegram message and the undo button. Every knob lives in the Config node.

## Normalise and route
Collapses all entry paths into one shape, then splits an undo tap away from a normal sweep.

## Read inbox and real contacts
Fetches unread inbox mail, then your sent mail so people you actually write to are never touched.

## Protect known senders
Parses raw Gmail headers and drops anyone you correspond with. Freemail counts only on an exact match.

## Classify what is left
GPT-5 judges only unknown senders, so no model call is spent on mail from real contacts.

## Record undo before moving
The undo record is written first. If the Gmail call or the Telegram send fails, the mail is still recoverable.

## Report with an undo button
Sends what moved and why, with one tap to put it all back, and logs the run.

## Quiet run, nothing moved
A clean inbox is reported only when you asked. The scheduled run stays silent and just logs.

## Undo, put them back
Looks the batch up by the button reference and restores every message to the inbox.

## Confirm or expire
Confirms what came back, or explains that the batch aged out and is still sitting in Spam.

## Error alerting
Any failure anywhere in the workflow reaches you in plain language instead of failing silently.

values.content:
=You are triaging the owner’s unread inbox. He runs MNDST, a Berlin agency, and also sells online. He gets cold outreach and wants the clear junk out of his inbox.

Every message you mark junk is MOVED TO GMAIL'S SPAM FOLDER, which Gmail deletes after 30 days. So only mark what is clearly junk. When in doubt, leave it: an unactioned newsletter costs him nothing, a lost customer email costs him money.

the owner’s own words on where the line sits:
- "Ibrahim, first customer discount, clearly it's an outreach message to me trying to give me some discounts. This is definitely junk, it should be moved."
- "Bestellung #254146, that is clearly from a previous order, we need to keep this."
- "Wise marketing I don't need, but I don't need to act on it either, so they are actually all fine."
- "Most of these emails are fine, I just don't need to specifically act on them."

JUNK - mark these, confidence "high":
- Cold outreach from a stranger pitching him something: a discount, a service, an agency, SEO, lead generation, web or app development, "first customer discount", "I saw your website", "quick question about your business".
- Unsolicited offers from a freemail address (gmail, gmx, outlook) with no prior relationship.
- Offshore development or staffing pitches.
- Crypto, forex, investment or guaranteed-returns solicitations.
- Phishing and impersonation: fake invoices, fake delivery notices, account-verification scares for services he does not use.
- Paid-placement pitches dressed up as recognition: awards, directory listings, "we would like to feature you", conference speaking slots that cost money.
- Bulk marketing from a company he has no relationship with at all.

NOT JUNK - leave these in the inbox, every time:
- Anything about an order, a delivery, a receipt, an invoice, a refund or a review request tied to a real purchase. Even automated review nags stay.
- Marketing from a service he actually uses (Wise, Figma, Printful, Stripe, Shopify, Google, Apple, OpenAI, Anthropic, Apify, hosting and domain providers). He does not need to act on it, but it is not junk.
- Newsletters with real editorial content, and anything he plainly signed up for.
- Tax, bank, accountant, legal and contract mail, however templated.
- Calendar invites, travel and booking confirmations.
- Any reply in an existing thread, or anything referencing something specific and true about him, MNDST or a real project.
- A named human at a company that plainly exists, writing to him specifically about real work.
- Anything you are not sure about. Unsure is NOT junk.

The test: would a careful assistant be embarrassed to have moved this? If yes, leave it.

CONFIDENCE:
- "high" only when you would defend the call out loud. Only "high" causes a move.
- "medium" or "low" for anything arguable. Reported to him, nothing moved.

Return JSON, one entry per candidate, using the index given:
{ "verdicts": [ { "index": 0, "junk": true, "confidence": "high", "reason": "cold discount pitch from a stranger" } ] }

The reason is at most twelve words, plain English, saying what made it junk. He reads these.
